approved_claim_dependencies.claim: For dashboard speed, expensive journey analytics can be calculated into a persisted dataset on a schedule rather than recalculating all historical engagement data on each page load.

notes: Read-only SQL verified PersistedDataset exists with refresh interval, schedule, result data, cache, Lava command, and build script columns.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: This Data Analytics Hub walkthrough describes a Rock-based journey engagement dashboard that combines content-channel journey definitions, group/member participation, group member attendance, campus filters, persisted datasets, and Lava chart shortcodes to help ministry teams evaluate engagement and improve content strategy.

This Digital Strategy Hub session adds practical LMS guidance from churches beginning to build training content in Rock. It treats LMS as a way to deliver volunteer and staff training, reuse existing teaching assets, and pair content with communications that invite people into structured learning rather than leaving training scattered across unrelated pages.
AI coaching should be framed as an assisted resource-routing layer with reviewable prompts, ministry-approved categories, and clear human oversight.

Publishing a ministry dashboard can change behavior when it exposes underused content or completion gaps; teams can then adjust marketing, launch timing, content length, and follow-up strategy based on observed engagement.

Journey reporting may need to join content-channel items, generated groups, group members, notes/comments, and attendance-style completion events because the ministry experience spans both content and group participation models.
LMS activity completion can interact with existing Rock concepts such as groups, group sync, and workflow actions, which makes LMS useful for volunteer training and operational follow-up.

notes: Read-only SQL verified LMS activity/completion tables, group/member tables, and workflow action surfaces that can support volunteer-training follow-up.
This verifies structural surfaces only, not a specific LMS implementation.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: When moving from another LMS into Rock, plan for differences in platform logic instead of assuming videos and lessons can be imported without redesign.
Online next-step pathways can combine dashboards, content, and LMS when the church defines the discipleship path being supported.

This Digital Strategy Hub session frames AI-assisted coaching and online learning as tools that still need ministry ownership. It connects LMS, dashboards, content, and mobile engagement to a discipleship path, while warning that AI should support reviewed coaching and resource routing rather than make ungoverned ministry decisions.
A binge-style content idea can become a structured learning path when the church defines sequence, purpose, and completion signals rather than only embedding videos.
Early LMS work should start with a few clear training use cases, such as volunteer or staff onboarding, before attempting a large content migration.
Engagement goals should be tied to the path the church wants people to take, not simply to whether a digital tool was launched.
Reusable communication sections and global style controls can reduce template drift when churches standardize common layouts, buttons, text styles, columns, and Lava/code blocks.

An LMS class can combine content acknowledgements, required video watching, quizzes, file uploads, and facilitator-scored activities, so training design should define both learner actions and staff review responsibilities.

notes: Read-only SQL verified LMS activity, class activity, completion, participant, comment, points, grading, file, and notification columns that support structured learner and facilitator actions.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: This February 2025 Media Watch session is a high-value public-safe source for Rock LMS and the new communications wizard direction. It explains LMS programs, courses, classes, learning plans, participants, on-demand versus academic-calendar modes, activity types, facilitator grading, availability rules, and workflow hooks, then demonstrates communications beta features such as topics, reachable-audience counts, starter templates, global styles, reusable sections, drag-and-drop blocks, image/column controls, and Lava/code blocks.
LMS is most valuable when the church treats it as part of a broader volunteer readiness system, not just a content repository.
Existing training videos can become Rock LMS activities, but completion, sequencing, and facilitator review should be configured intentionally around the desired learner outcome.

notes: Read-only SQL verified LMS course/class/activity/completion surfaces and workflow completion hooks used to structure training outcomes.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: A journey dashboard can define completion as finishing every day in a journey, then use group member attendance and participation records to compare completion across solo, group, spouse, campus, demographic, and journey-category dimensions.

This Digital Strategy Hub session adds implementation-oriented LMS guidance from a church activating the LMS engine and migrating content from another learning platform. It is useful for planning how existing videos and course material can be restructured into Rock LMS while preserving the ministry logic of training paths, groups, and volunteer readiness.

The communications beta wizard introduces topic tagging and reachable-audience counts by medium, helping senders choose email, SMS, or push based on actual contactability rather than only the size of a communication list.

Rock LMS organizes training into programs, courses, class instances, learning plans, activities, and learning participants, with the program deciding whether the experience is on-demand or academic-calendar based.

notes: Read-only SQL verified Rock LMS program, course, class, activity, participant, semester, completion, and configuration-mode surfaces.

approved_claim_dependencies.claim: Existing teaching series or training videos can become LMS content, but teams should still design the course path, completion expectations, and follow-up communication around the learner.
